name: Amanda Foster
chief_complaint: Feeling very low in mood, no energy, can't seem to enjoy anything anymore
opening_statement: I've been feeling really down for about 3 months now. I can't concentrate at work, I'm not sleeping well, and I've lost interest in things I used to enjoy. I feel worthless and like I'm letting everyone down. Sometimes I think everyone would be better off without me.
emotional_baseline: Flat affect, poor eye contact, tearful at times, cooperative with interview

symptoms.symptom: Persistent low mood (anhedonia - loss of pleasure)

socrates.onset: Gradual onset 3 months ago, progressively worsening
socrates.character: Persistent sadness, emptiness, inability to feel pleasure (anhedonia)
socrates.associated: Insomnia, fatigue, poor concentration, feelings of worthlessness, passive suicidal ideation
socrates.timing: Persistent throughout day, worse mornings (diurnal variation)
socrates.relieving: No relief, cannot be cheered up by positive events

rag_citation.source: eTG Psychiatry 9.1.1: Major Depressive Disorder - Diagnostic Criteria
rag_citation.quote: Major depression requires ≥2 weeks of depressed mood OR anhedonia, plus ≥5 of 9 DSM-5 criteria (sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor, suicidal ideation)

socrates.onset: Started 3 months ago with mood decline
socrates.character: Difficulty falling asleep + waking 3-4am unable to return to sleep (early morning wakening - biological symptom)
socrates.relieving: None - cannot fall back asleep after 3-4am waking
socrates.severity: Severe - chronic sleep deprivation worsening mood/function

rag_citation.quote: Early morning wakening (2-3h before usual) is characteristic biological symptom of major depression

symptoms.symptom: Passive suicidal ideation (thoughts of death WITHOUT plan/intent)

socrates.character: Thoughts that 'everyone would be better off without me', passive death wish, NO active plan or intent to act

rag_citation.quote: Assess suicidality: ideation (passive vs active), plan, intent, means, protective factors - passive ideation still warrants close monitoring
Fatigue and loss of energy (anergia) are core neurovegetative symptoms of depression - present in 90% of cases
Impaired concentration and decision-making ability are cognitive symptoms of depression - affect work performance

symptoms.symptom: Feelings of worthlessness and excessive guilt

rag_citation.quote: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive/inappropriate guilt distinguish major depression from adjustment disorder

family_history: Mother has depression (on sertraline). No family history of bipolar disorder or psychosis. No family history of completed suicide.

social_history.alcohol: Increased recently - drinking 1-2 glasses wine nightly (self-medicating sleep/mood), previously social drinker only
social_history.occupation: High school teacher (on sick leave past 2 weeks - unable to function at work)
social_history.relationship: Divorced 6 months ago (stressor precipitating depression), 2 children (ages 8 and 10) living with ex-husband
social_history.living_situation: Lives alone in apartment, sees children weekends
social_history.support: Limited social support - isolated from friends during depression, supportive sister

mental_state_examination.appearance: Unkempt, poor hygiene, appears older than stated age, psychomotor retardation evident
mental_state_examination.behavior: Cooperative, poor eye contact, slumped posture, slow movements
mental_state_examination.speech: Slow rate, low volume, reduced spontaneity, latency in responses
mental_state_examination.affect_objective: Flat affect, restricted range, congruent with depressed mood, tearful when discussing divorce/children
mental_state_examination.thought_form: Logical, coherent, no formal thought disorder
mental_state_examination.thought_content: Negative automatic thoughts ('I'm a failure', 'I'm worthless'), passive suicidal ideation (NO active plan, NO intent, NO access to means), rumination about divorce/loss of children, NO psychotic features (delusions/hallucinations)
mental_state_examination.cognition: Alert, oriented to time/place/person, impaired concentration
mental_state_examination.insight: PARTIAL insight - recognizes feeling unwell, ambivalent about treatment ('nothing will help')

physical_examination.vitals: HR 72 bpm, BP 118/74 mmHg, BMI 21 (weight loss 5kg over 3 months)
physical_examination.neurological: Normal cranial nerves, motor, sensory, reflexes - no organic neurological cause

investigations.tsh: 2.1 mIU/L (normal - hypothyroidism adequately treated, not causing depression)
investigations.fbc: Hemoglobin 132 g/L, WCC 7.2 x10⁹/L (normal - no anemia)
investigations.lft: Normal liver function (no alcohol-related liver disease yet)
investigations.phq9: PHQ-9 score 19/27 (MODERATELY SEVERE depression - threshold for treatment)

expected_diagnosis: Major Depressive Disorder (moderate-severe) - DSM-5 criteria met (7/9 symptoms × 3 months)
expected_management: - Ideation: Passive death wish ✓ ('better off without me')
- Means: NO access to lethal means ✓
- Protective factors: Children (motivation to live), sister (support) ✓
- Risk level: MODERATE risk (passive ideation + severe depression + recent stressor)
- Decision: Safe for outpatient management WITH close follow-up (review 1 week, crisis plan, sister involved)
- Crisis contacts: Sister (phone), Lifeline 13 11 14, GP after-hours
- Safety contract: Agree to contact crisis line if ideation worsens
- Sertraline 50mg daily (start low) → increase to 100-200mg after 1-2 weeks
- Side effects: Nausea (transient), sexual dysfunction (common), initial activation/anxiety (rare)
- BLACK BOX WARNING: Monitor for suicidal ideation increase in first 2-4 weeks (age <25, reassure 42yo)
4. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) OR Interpersonal Therapy (IPT):
- Referral to psychologist (MBS Mental Health Care Plan - up to 10 sessions/year)
- Target: Negative automatic thoughts ('I'm worthless'), behavioral activation (re-engage activities)
- Regular sleep-wake times, avoid alcohol (worsens depression), limit screens before bed
- Consider short-term temazepam 10mg nocte PRN (max 2-4 weeks - avoid dependence)
- Exercise prescription: 30 min moderate exercise 5×/week (equivalent to antidepressant for mild-moderate depression)
- Reduce alcohol (currently using as self-medication - worsens depression)
- Vitamin D supplementation 1000 IU daily (mildly deficient)
- Medical certificate for sick leave (2-4 weeks initially)
- Graduated return to work when improving (phased return)
9. Use PHQ-9 to track response (target <5 for remission)
10. Monitor for bipolar disorder (antidepressants can trigger mania - rare, but ask about previous hypomania)
HOSPITAL ADMISSION CRITERIA (NOT met this case):
12. Continue antidepressant 6-12 months AFTER remission (relapse prevention)
13. Relapse prevention: Maintain CBT skills, exercise, sleep hygiene
14. If recurrent depression (≥3 episodes): Consider long-term maintenance antidepressant

critical_errors.error: Missed active suicidal plan/intent (patient discharged without safety assessment)
critical_errors.explanation: Active suicidal plan + intent requires IMMEDIATE psychiatric assessment +/- hospitalization - discharge is negligent

critical_errors.error: Failed to screen for organic causes (TSH, B12, anemia) before diagnosing primary depression
critical_errors.explanation: Hypothyroidism, B12 deficiency, anemia can mimic depression - must exclude before starting antidepressants

critical_errors.error: Prescribed antidepressant WITHOUT psychological therapy (medication alone insufficient)
critical_errors.explanation: Combination of medication + CBT superior to either alone in moderate-severe depression - both essential

critical_errors.error: Failed to warn about SSRI 2-4 week lag time for effect (patient stops medication prematurely)
critical_errors.explanation: Many patients discontinue SSRIs after 1-2 weeks expecting immediate effect - education prevents premature discontinuation

critical_errors.error: Prescribed tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) as first-line (instead of SSRI)
critical_errors.explanation: SSRIs preferred over TCAs (better tolerability, safer in overdose) - TCAs reserved for SSRI failures

critical_errors.error: Stopped antidepressant immediately after symptom resolution (instead of 6-12 month continuation)
critical_errors.explanation: Early discontinuation increases relapse risk to 50-80% - continue 6-12 months after remission for relapse prevention

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent - realistic major depression presentation with DSM-5 criteria clearly met, appropriate suicide risk assessment outlined
fracp_reviews.difficulty_appropriate: Yes - Medium difficulty appropriate (suicide risk assessment, treatment decision-making)
fracp_reviews.rag_citations_correct: Yes - eTG 9.1 citations verified and accurate
fracp_reviews.feedback: Excellent psychiatry persona. Good emphasis on suicide risk assessment (ideation/plan/intent/means/protective factors framework). Biological symptoms well-described (early morning wakening, psychomotor retardation). Consider adding brief mention of Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) for formal risk assessment tool.

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRANZCP, Consultation-liaison psychiatry subspecialist, 15 years post-fellowship
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate depression management - appropriate combination of SSRI + CBT, organic screening performed
fracp_reviews.feedback: Good persona. Management pathway correct (safety assessment → SSRI + CBT → close follow-up). Excellent inclusion of organic screening (TSH, B12) before diagnosing primary depression. Suggest mentioning PHQ-9 score explicitly (19/27 = moderately severe - threshold for combined pharmacotherapy + psychotherapy).

learning_objectives: Diagnose major depression using DSM-5 criteria (≥5/9 symptoms × ≥2 weeks including depressed mood OR anhedonia)
Conduct comprehensive suicide risk assessment (ideation, plan, intent, means, previous attempts, protective factors)
Differentiate passive suicidal ideation (moderate risk, outpatient) from active plan/intent (high risk, hospitalization)
Prescribe SSRI first-line (sertraline 50-200mg) with appropriate patient education (2-4 week lag, 6-12 month continuation)
Combine pharmacotherapy with psychological therapy (CBT or IPT - combination superior to either alone)
Screen for organic causes before diagnosing primary depression (TSH, B12, anemia)
Create crisis plan (remove means, crisis contacts, safety contract, involve supports)
Understand biological symptoms of depression (early morning wakening, psychomotor retardation, weight loss)
